title: "Wildfire prediction as an application of pre-season drought information"
output: html_document

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)
metrics <- read.csv("outputs/forecast-check-metrics.csv")
u <- read.csv("outputs/forecast-skill-uncertainty.csv")
```

## Corrected target and evaluation design

The response is May–July wildfire count. All, Human, and Natural are fitted
separately with negative binomial models. The drought predictor is April 30
moisture deficit in centimeters. The old notebook trained a natural-fire model
but compared it against all-fire observations; that mismatch is corrected.
Expanding training windows contain only preceding eligible seasons, beginning
with 15 seasons. These are retrospective hindcasts, not forecasts issued in
real time. Source-publication delays are not reconstructed.

$$\log E[N_y] = \beta_0 + \beta_1 D_y.$$

## Forecast skill and its uncertainty

```{r metrics}
knitr::kable(metrics, digits=3)
```

Climatology is an intercept-only negative binomial baseline. TimeTrend uses
calendar year; DroughtAndTime includes both predictors. All models are compared
on identical evaluation years for each cause. The additional specifications
are sensitivity checks, not independently validated model-selection winners.

```{r uncertainty}
knitr::kable(u, digits=3)
```

Positive MAEImprovement means drought beats climatology. The 95% intervals use
2,000 paired circular moving-block bootstrap resamples of the evaluation years
with three-year blocks and a fixed seed. With only 15 evaluation seasons,
these intervals remain approximate. They resample existing hindcast errors,
not the complete estimation and model-selection process.

```{r hindcasts}
knitr::include_graphics("outputs/hindcasts.png")
```

Natural-fire point estimates improve over climatology, but their paired
uncertainty interval includes no improvement. This supports a measured
application section, rather than making predictive skill the central claim.

## Conditional count intervals and later seasons

```{r forecasts}
if (file.exists("outputs/forecasts.csv")) knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/forecasts.csv"), digits=2)
```

Later-season estimates use archived April weather beyond the fire database's
last outcome year. They are retrospective reconstructions with unassessed
outcomes. The 90% negative binomial intervals condition on fitted coefficients
and dispersion; they do not include parameter uncertainty. Independently fitted
cause-specific means need not add to the All model's mean.

## Previous burn area and Bayesian extensions

`outputs/prior-burn-hindcasts.csv` checks the original prior-burn question using
a properly aligned May 1–April 30 antecedent window and a common evaluation set.
Final reported fire sizes are not necessarily available at that forecast date;
this is a sensitivity analysis, not an operationally reconstructed predictor.

`scripts/bayesian.R` preserves separate Bayesian count fits with explicit priors,
four chains, seeds, and saved posterior predictive draws. It requires optional
`brms` and a working Stan toolchain. Those fits were not run during modernization.
The original exploratory exponential acreage fit is retained in `archive/legacy/`;
it is not treated as a validated burned-area forecast.
